name: Tecture IO
description:
Tecture IO is a zero-configuration viewer for file-based architecture diagrams authored by coding agents. The entire product ships as one npm package — @tecture/core — that boots a single Express process on port 3000 and serves both a REST API over the user's local ./architecture directory and a bundled React UI that renders the graph.

The repo is a pnpm monorepo with three packages: @tecture/core (the CLI + HTTP API + library entry, the only published deployable), @tecture/web (the React + Vite + ReactFlow UI, bundled into the server at build time), and @tecture/shared (TypeScript types that define the file format and the API contract between server and UI). The data layer is split behind two interfaces — ArchitectureDataSource and LayoutStore — so the same routes and UI can be reused over alternate backends.

The package exposes both a CLI binary (the default UX, read-and-write filesystem) and a library entry (createApp, the interfaces, error classes, and the FS implementations) for downstream projects that want to embed Tecture against a different source — for example, a viewer that fetches architecture files from the GitHub API instead of disk.

There are no datastores, no authentication, and no external services called from the CLI — the only durable state is the flat tree of JSON + Markdown files in the developer's own repository. Coding agents author that tree with ordinary fs.writeFile calls; the viewer reads it on demand.
